entities.summary: Anastassia Yehudith Michaeli (Hebrew: אנסטסיה מיכאלי, Russian: Анастасия Михаэли ; born 12 July 1975) is an Israeli journalist, television presenter, and politician. She served as a member of Knesset for Yisrael Beiteinu between 2009 and 2013. During her Knesset term she received media attention for attempting to physically disturb an Arab representative's speech and for comments she made on the psychology of gays and lesbians. While in the Knesset she was active in the international arena as chairperson of several parliamentary friendship leagues and represented the Knesset in official delegations to the European Union, France, Great Britain and Taiwan.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a member of Knesset and chairperson of parliamentary friendship leagues, Anastassia Michaeli played a role in shaping Israel's international relations with several European countries. Her actions had regional significance, contributing to the country's diplomatic landscape.
